## Hero-versus-hero matrix (5 of the same hero per side, 24 matches per pair, sides alternated)

Rows beat columns at the rate shown. The draft rule "never the same hero twice on one team" cannot hold with a 4-hero prototype pool, so duplicates are allowed. Five of one hero also forces roles the hero would not normally take, so this is a stress test, not a target. It shows that stacking Hollow Cartographers (area damage) is dominant; with the full 11-hero roster the no-duplicates rule removes this.

| Row beats column | cartographer | miko | revenant | smelter |
| ---------------- | ------------ | ---- | -------- | ------- |
| cartographer     | -            | 79%  | 71%      | 79%     |
| miko             | 21%          | -    | 21%      | 21%     |
| revenant         | 29%          | 79%  | -        | 33%     |
| smelter          | 21%          | 79%  | 67%      | -       |

## Catch-up experiment (cursed items)

500 matches per arm, seeds 3000-3499. Comeback rate = share of matches won by the team that was behind in net worth after phase 1.

| Arm                                            | Comeback rate |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Cursed items off (`curse.threshold = 0`)       | 31.8%         |
| Cursed items on, first boon values             | 32.8%         |
| Cursed items on, final boon values (committed) | 38.4%         |

The first boon values did not move comebacks. The committed values add about 6.6 points, roughly 2 standard errors. This is a first read only.
